correctness.rationale: Cylinder fixed points require p=2πm; negative cosine is the only possible sink. The strict Schur criterion for determinant b∈(0,1) gives exactly |d_m|<K and K²-d_m²<4(1+b)². Window overlap yields necessary and sufficient squared-integer spans; optimal K is attained in nonempty open intervals. Endpoints λ=±1 excluded; complete analytic proof and exact finite cross-check included.

originality.rationale: Exact strict maximum and even/odd threshold staircase was not located in the performed statement-level semantic and primary-source comparisons. The closest same-map transport theorem supplies drift bounds but not this count. The 1978 full text concerns chaotic attractors; 2015 numerical coexistence data provide context. Originality is best-knowledge only: inaccessible 1991 and 2011 full articles may imply some claims.
residual_risks: Wenzel–Biham–Jayaprakash (1991) full text could contain an equivalent multi-winding formula not visible in its abstract.
Celletti–Di Ruzza (2011) full text may derive sufficient general drift/Arnold-tongue criteria implying all or part of these period-one thresholds.
Older local-stability formulas are likely known; the claim of originality is focused on the simultaneous, sharp-maximizing integer staircase, not on any individual Jacobian inequality.

value.rationale: The number of simultaneously attracting period-one winding modes is a natural dynamical multistability invariant. Its exact forcing-optimized maximum over infinitely many winding possibilities, interlaced strict thresholds and weak-damping growth rate quantitatively classify a phenomenon previously documented mainly by numerical attractor inventories; the claim avoids higher-period and basin assertions.
